newsitem.title: USA: Gingrich seeks probe of Mexico drug czar.
newsitem.headline: Gingrich seeks probe of Mexico drug czar.

text.p: U.S. House of Representatives Speaker Newt Gingrich on Tuesday called for an investigation to determine if jailed Mexican drug czar Jesus Gutierrez Rebollo passed on information that could endanger U.S. drug agents.

Gingrich, a Georgia Republican, and House Republican Leader Dick Armey of Texas asked the House Intelligence Committee to find out what damage Gutierrez might have done to the U.S.-Mexican counternarcotics effort.

"We request that you urgently investigate this situation, beginning immediately with an assessment of the risks to the lives of American officials whose role in the drug war may have been revealed to the drug cartels by Gen. Gutierrez," Gingrich and Armey wrote House Intelligence Committee Chairman Porter Goss, a Florida Republican.
Gutierrez was arrested two weeks ago after only 10 weeks on the job for allegedly taking bribes from a drug kingpin.

President Bill Clinton last Friday recertified Mexico as an ally in the war against drugs and praised President Ernesto Zedillo for the arrest of Gutierrez and other Mexican officials. Decertification could have led to U.S. economic sanctions.
Clinton's action drew strong criticism from both Democrats and Republicans. Resolutions to overturn the certification have been introduced in the Senate and are being considered in the House.
Clinton could veto such a resolution if it passed Congress and it would then need a two-thirds majority in both chambers to take effect.

"It is clear that at least with regard to stemming the floodtide of drugs through Mexico and into our communities, the Clinton administration's policymaking and intelligence gathering system is broken. We believe it is our responsibility to do everything we can to clean up this mess," Gingrich and Armey said in their letter.
